note: Upper bounds in milliseconds for tests/latency-browser-check.js, one set per machine, because the same code takes different times on different machines and browsers (creator request 2026-10-18, after the PC's budgets judged a run on the Windows laptop). tests/latency-machine.txt, not committed, names the machine running the check. Creator decision 2026-09-26: limits sit at today's real times, not generous ones; any real slowdown must fail. *WorkMs is how long the game's own handlers ran for that input, which only our code affects; the matching *Ms is input to the first task after the next frame, which also includes up to one 60 Hz frame (16.7 ms) of waiting, so a click must show within two frames (34 ms). Tighten when the code gets faster; loosen only by recorded creator decision.

linux-pc.note: The creator's Linux PC. Set 2026-09-26 just above the worst of three Firefox runs (Chromium is faster everywhere). Tightened 2026-10-20 just above the worst of three Firefox runs of 345ab4a, after the left stats panel was removed: startup 496-516 ms (535-570 before), switching to Expert 7-9 ms of work and 12-13 to screen (8-11 and 13-16 since 2026-10-19, 16-19 and 18-22 before), the freeze after a game ends 68-77 (74-91). expertWinResultsMs added 2026-10-26 (creator decision: time a long Expert win to its full results, the analysis workers included), set just above the worst of three Firefox runs: 216, 224, 216 ms for a 229-click win, of which the reports worker's finished-game took about 100 ms. Tightened 2026-10-26 just above the worst of six Firefox runs, after the result charts' dots moved from SVG circles to one canvas per chart (13,149 circles had made every page layout cost about 40 ms) and the reports worker began proving positions during play: new game 7-13 ms of work (22-27 before) and 11-18 to screen, the freeze after a game ends 33-66 ms, and expertWinResultsMs 132-152 ms (finished-game replies 58-73 ms after it is posted). The freeze now counts every interval of the 10 ms timer; until 2026-10-26 only intervals over 50 ms counted, so these runs would have read 0-66. Startup tightened 2026-10-26 just above the worst of three Firefox runs, after saved boards and square lists became strings: 244-257 ms (523-528 before). Progressive results (creator decision 2026-11-03: "display things as they come in, so nothing blocks other stuff ... as long as the user isn't blocked, budgets can be raised"): the result's parts show as their data arrives. The same day the check's Expert game began placing one flag: the synthetic Expert wins all have flags, so the flagless win had been ranked among no-mark wins alone, by itself, and drew no charts; with the flag its results rank it among 1,576 wins and draw every chart. expertWinResultsMs, the time to the last part, was raised to 525, just above the worst of nine Firefox runs of the final code that day at system load 2.8-5.1 (386-520 ms; the code before took 448-527 in eleven runs alternating with it, every part waiting for the slowest). The decision holds only while the player is not blocked, so three budgets were added the same day, just above the worst of those nine runs: the winning click's own work (2-4 ms), its time to screen (17-25 ms; the two-frame 34 ms like every click), and the longest freeze in the two seconds after it (32-54 ms in ten runs, the tenth a check of the game's clicks; the code before 30-61 in the alternating runs). Its longest single frame is live perf charts' first draw, about 27 ms; the longer readings are short result tasks back to back, each placement's forced layout at most 12 ms. The freeze after a game ends was tightened the same day from 70 to 35, just above the same runs' 26-31 ms (the code before 34-45).

windows-laptop.note: The creator's Windows laptop. Set 2026-10-18 just above the worst of five Firefox 155 runs of release d211d15 (four in one sitting, one earlier that evening), leaving out Firefox's first launch on this machine (startup 1704, firstClickWorkMs 44); on mains power, the Balanced power plan, with other programs keeping the processor about 40% busy. The click time-to-screen budgets keep the two-frame 34 ms except clickMs, which reached 36 ms here (38). Its times vary far more than the PC's, so these budgets catch only large slowdowns: across the five runs startup took 1276-2306 ms, new game work 29-55, newGameMs 36-219, and the after-game freeze 89-198. expertWinResultsMs (added 2026-10-26) and winClickWorkMs, winClickMs, and afterWinFreezeMs (added 2026-11-03) have no budgets here yet: until they are set just above the worst of three runs on this machine, the check fails here, printing its measurements.
